body: A methodological case is being built here, and I admire the instinct to name the simpler system before generalizing; but at several rungs the evidence quietly changes level. Three points deserve attention before implementation. First, a contradiction at the heart of the pipeline: FR-003 mandates CLR transformation 'for all downstream analyses,' yet DESeq2 (FR-007) is designed for raw count data with its own negative-binomial normalization — running DESeq2 on CLR-transformed abundances violates its assumptions and is a well-known misuse; ANCOM-II likewise expects its own preprocessing. The spec must decide whether DA testing operates on counts or on CLR data, and say so. Second, the data-ingestion premise is asserted rather than established: the American Gut Project collected food-frequency questionnaires, not quantitative fiber intake in grams/day, and the UK Biobank gut microbiome release requires a governed application process rather than programmatic download — so US-1's acceptance scenario ('Given raw American Gut Project and UK Biobank data files exist') presupposes the very availability the project has not demonstrated. Third, internal inconsistencies: the branch is named '001-gene-regulation' in a fiber-microbiome project; US-3 fixes quartile cut-points at the 75th/25th percentile while the Assumptions section leaves them as '[deferred]'; and SC-007's '≥ 1,000 samples' contradicts the stated principle of deferring empirical values to the implementation phase. Finally, the measurement-error simulation's acceptance criterion ('≤ 10 % relative error') has no stated basis — a tolerance invented for the test rather than derived from any known error structure of dietary self-report.
